To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the taxonomy independent binning methods can be divided into two main categories based on the feature they use for binning.

(1) the taxonomy independent methods for binning of metagenomic sequences are the only way for the reconstruction of novel genomes from the shotgun metagenomic data; (2) the binning of short sequences is still challenging and requires more research; (3) the initial assembly of the metagenome is a prerequisite for binning of short reads; and (4) the visualization of metagenomic data is a powerful tool for gaining insight into the structure of the microbial community.

the binning strategies are divided into two categories based on their principle, the taxonomy independent methods are based on clustering of the features extracted from the sequence, the taxonomy dependent methods require prior knowledge and are based on homology inference against the reference databases, and the length of the sequences has a crucial role in the choice of binning strategy
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new bioinformatic tools for binning and analysis of metagenomic data.
the analysis of metagenomic data from various environments,
the development and improvement of the bioinformatics tools and algorithms for the analysis of the metatranscriptomic and metagenomic datasets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no universal solution for the binning problem and the selection of a particular method is dependent on the type of metagenomic data and the goals of the analysis.

the taxonomy independent methods are more flexible and can be utilized for the binning of short sequences as well, while they are still not able to compete with taxonomy dependent methods in terms of the accuracy of binning.
the binning methods are not a silver bullet and the choice of method should be based on the type of the metagenome data, as well as the goal of the study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reference-free methods are more flexible, but require longer reads.
the taxonomy independent binning is still a very active area in the field of computational biology and the number of methods is constantly increasing.
the reference-free binners are still in their infancy and require more attention from bioinformaticians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a novel, universal binning method that is capable of handling the short sequences and is able to perform binning on both assembled and unassembled metagenomic data.
taxonomy independent binning is an essential step in a metagenomic data analysis, and that it is a promising tool for the analysis of metagenomic data.
the reference-free binners are still in their early development, and therefore the current state of the art in metagenomic analysis is still based on the use of the reference-based methods.
